subject: Encryption & KMS requirements — follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Martinez <sofia@paywise.com>, PayWise Security Team <security@paywise.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-29T15:08:00Z
Subject: Re: Encryption & KMS requirements — follow-up and next steps

Thanks again for the call earlier — great to meet the PayWise team. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on the encryption and key management items we discussed:

Call recap (high level)
- In-transit: TLS (mTLS optional), endpoints exposed over TLS 1.2+ (we recommend 1.3).
- At-rest: platform volume + object encryption by default (AES-256).
- CMEK / BYOK: we support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS providers and HSM-backed integrations; keys can be used to envelope-encrypt model artifacts and persisted KV/cache.
- Key rotation: support for scheduled rotation; can be orchestrated by customer or Redwood (per policy).
- Audit & logging: detailed KMS operation logs + access/audit trails; we ship audit events to customer audit sinks on request.
- Data residency & retention: data can be pinned to region; retention controls configurable per-route.

Open questions / actions for PayWise
1) Priority: please confirm whether HSM-backed keys are a hard requirement or if cloud-KMS with HSM (e.g., AWS KMS with CloudHSM) is acceptable.
2) Scope: which data categories do you expect to encrypt with CMEK (models, stored user content, logs)?
3) Rotation/compromise policy: what rotation cadence and compromise response do you need (e.g., 90d rotation + emergency revoke)?
4) Network: procurement needs IP allowlist & egress details — we can share an allowlist CSV.

Attachments we can provide immediately: SOC2_Summary.pdf, short KMS integration guide, audit logging sample.

Suggested next steps
- Technical deep-dive (45min) with Dev (solutions) to walk KMS integration options and HSM details — propose Tue 2027-03-30 10:00 PT.
- Dev to share KMS integration guide and sample config prior to meeting.

If you can confirm the HSM requirement and preferred time, I’ll get the invite out.

Thanks,

From: Sofia Martinez <sofia@paywise.com>

Subject: Re: Encryption & KMS requirements — follow-up and next steps

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our security team before the deep-dive:

1) HSM requirement: PayWise requires FIPS 140-2 level 3 HSMs for any keys that protect PII at rest. If Redwood can integrate with a customer-managed HSM (either on-cloud or on-prem via a key-wrap model), that will satisfy our requirement.
2) Key exportability: keys must not be exportable in plaintext from the HSM. We need to understand if Redwood ever holds unwrapped keys or can operate with wrapped keys only.
3) mTLS: for intra-service traffic we prefer mTLS; for public API endpoints mutual TLS would be ideal but may be optional if other compensating controls exist.
4) Audit logs: we need tamper-evident audit logs for key usage (key-id, operation, principal, timestamp). Can logs be delivered to our SIEM?
5) Retention & deletion: if a customer requests deletion, what data is purged vs retained for audit purposes? Need details on deletion workflow and timing.

We attached a short question matrix (PayWise_KMS_Questions.xlsx) — can you have your engineering team respond inline or during the deep-dive?

We are available for the technical deep-dive Tue 2027-03-30 10:00 PT. Please send a calendar invite and any pre-read.

Sofia Martinez
Head of Security Programs | PayWise
sofia@paywise.com

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Martinez <sofia@paywise.com>, PayWise Security Team <security@paywise.com>

Subject: Re: Encryption & KMS requirements — follow-up and next steps

Hi Sofia — appreciate the detail. Quick answers up front, followed by a few technical notes and attachments I’m sharing prior to the call.

Short answers
- HSM support: yes — Redwood supports customer-managed HSMs via several integration patterns: (1) native cloud-KMS CMEK (AWS KMS backed by CloudHSM, GCP External Key Manager) and (2) external HSMs via key-wrap / KMIP or PKCS#11 gateways where the customer retains key material. We do not require plaintext key import into Redwood.
- Key export: we do not store plaintext private key material from customer HSMs. For envelope encryption we store ciphertext/blobs; key operations are proxied to the customer KMS/HSM.
- mTLS & in-transit: public API endpoints are TLS 1.2+; we support mutual TLS for private/dedicated deployments and can layer mTLS on top of our service mesh for intra-cluster traffic.
- Audit logs: we generate detailed KMS operation logs (key-id, operation, principal, request-id, timestamp). We can forward logs to customer SIEM via syslog/HTTPS or push to a customer S3/GCS bucket. Logs are sequential and include HMACed integrity markers for tamper detection on request.
- Deletion: deletion workflow is documented — on customer request we wipe persisted blobs and metadata according to configured retention windows (typically: immediate purge for ephemeral content, configurable 30/90/365d for persisted artifacts). Audit records of the deletion event are retained for compliance unless otherwise agreed.

Attachments (attached to this thread)
- redwood-kms-integration-guide.pdf (integration patterns, supported providers, sample requests)
- redwood-audit-logging-snippet.txt (sample log lines and forwarding config)

Sample configuration snippet for CMEK (example)
``
kms: {
  provider: aws_kms,
  key_id: "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01-2345",
  mode: envelope, // Redwood stores ciphertext; KMS performs unwrap
  rotation: { automatic: true, window_days: 90 }
}
``

Network & allowlist
- I’ll attach an allowlist CSV in the shared drive link; we can provide fixed egress IP ranges for Dedicated and Private deployments.

Next steps
- Join the deep-dive Tue 10:00 PT. I’ll walk the integration guide and we can confirm HSM patterns PayWise prefers.
